en: Up to date with the latest news or developments; side by side
hook: A-BREAST: chest to chest, side by side, keeping pace.
story: Abreast. Up to date with the latest news or developments; also, side by side. Every morning, Cole's grandfather reads three newspapers on the veranda with his tea, then listens to the radio news at noon. At eighty, he knows more about world events than his grandsons. He likes to keep abreast of everything. In the evening, the two of them stroll abreast along the river, arguing about politics. Abreast literally means breast to breast, side by side, so keeping abreast of the news means keeping pace with it. So, what word means staying fully up to date? ... Abreast.

gre.s: Researchers in such a fast-moving field must read constantly to stay ____ of new findings; otherwise their own work can become obsolete within months.
gre.clue: otherwise their own work can become obsolete within months

example: Farida reads three newspapers on her morning commute to keep abreast of the cricket board's latest selection decisions.

en: Showing selfless concern for the well-being of others
hook: ALTRUISTIC: ALTER (other) + TRUE care for others.
story: Altruistic. Showing selfless concern for the well-being of others. Every winter, Mitch's mother collects old blankets from her whole building. She washes them, mends the torn ones, and goes at night to the railway station to give them to people sleeping in the cold. She never posts a photo or tells anyone. Her kindness is purely altruistic. Altruistic comes from the Latin alter, meaning other, as in alternative, so an altruistic person lives for others. So, what word describes kindness that expects nothing in return? ... Altruistic.

gre.s: Although the donor claimed his motives were purely ____, critics noted that the gift earned him an enormous tax deduction.
gre.clue: the gift earned him an enormous tax deduction

example: Rahim's altruistic decision to donate a kidney to a stranger inspired dozens of people in his neighborhood to register as organ donors.

en: Without a clear shape, form, or structure
hook: A-MORPH-ous: 'a' means without, 'morph' means shape. Without shape.
story: Amorphous. Without a clear shape, form, or structure. At the first meeting of their startup, Frank and his friends talked for three hours about apps, delivery, farming and education, but nobody could say what the business actually was. Their plan was amorphous, like a cloud drifting over the river. Their mentor [chuckle] gave them one week to choose a single idea. A means without and morph means shape, as in morphing, so amorphous means without shape. So, what word describes a plan with no clear form? ... Amorphous.

gre.s: The committee's proposal remained frustratingly ____: it gestured toward reform but specified no budget, no timeline, and no responsible agency.
gre.clue: specified no budget, no timeline, and no responsible agency

example: The protest movement remained amorphous for months, with no leaders, no headquarters, and no agreed list of demands.

en: Deviating from what is normal or expected
hook: A-NOMAL-ous: 'a-normal', not normal.
story: Anomalous. Deviating from what is normal or expected. Mango trees flower in late winter and give fruit in summer. But one year, Steve's grandfather found a single tree heavy with tiny green mangoes in December. Neighbours came from three villages to see it. A botanist from the university said the anomalous tree may have been confused by unusual weather. An anomaly is something that does not fit the pattern, so anomalous means out of the ordinary. So, what word describes something that breaks from the normal pattern? ... Anomalous.

gre.s: Because every other sample showed the same chemical signature, researchers dismissed the one ____ reading as the result of contamination.
gre.clue: every other sample showed the same chemical signature

example: An anomalous spike in electricity use every midnight led auditors to discover an illegal cryptocurrency mining rig in the basement.

en: Something that is the exact reverse of another thing
hook: ANTI-THESIS: against the thesis, the exact opposite.
story: Antithesis. Something that is the exact reverse of another thing. Sam's two grandmothers could not be more different. One lives in a quiet hill village, rises at dawn, and speaks softly to her plants. The other lives in a busy city flat, stays up late watching cricket, and [laugh] shouts at every umpire. Each is the antithesis of the other, yet both love Sam fiercely. Anti means against and thesis means a position, so an antithesis stands directly against something. So, what word names the exact opposite of another thing? ... Antithesis.

gre.s: The minimalist new museum, with its bare white walls and empty spaces, is the ____ of the ornate palace that once stood on the site.
gre.clue: bare white walls and empty spaces

example: Shy and soft-spoken, the new captain was the antithesis of his loud predecessor, yet the players responded to him just as well.

en: The classic example of a type; the original pattern others copy
hook: ARCH-TYPE: the ARCH (chief, first) TYPE.
story: Archetype. The classic example of a type; the original pattern others copy. When people picture an old village schoolteacher, many imagine the same figure: an old man in a white shirt and thick glasses, walking to school with a black umbrella, strict in class but kind afterwards. Sean's grandfather fit that picture exactly. He was the archetype of the village teacher. Arch means first or chief, as in archbishop, so an archetype is the first model that others follow. So, what word names the classic, original example of a type? ... Archetype.

gre.s: The scheming stepmother of old folk tales is the ____ from which countless later villains, in novels and films alike, have been copied.
gre.clue: from which countless later villains

example: For many Bangladeshi readers, Himu has become the archetype of the carefree young man drifting through Dhaka in a yellow panjabi.

en: Showing bold willingness to take risks; daringly bold (sometimes rude)
hook: AUDACIOUS: 'AUDACity' — the nerve to do something bold.
story: Audacious. Showing bold willingness to take risks; daringly bold, sometimes rude. At nineteen, Leah walked into the office of a famous city fashion designer without an appointment, laid her sketches on his desk, and offered to work for free for one month to prove herself. The receptionist [gasp] froze. The designer stared, then smiled, and hired her that afternoon. It was an audacious move. Audacious comes from the Latin for dare, the same root as audacity, the nerve to try something bold. So, what word describes a daringly bold act? ... Audacious.

gre.s: The startup's ____ plan to compete directly with three established giants struck investors as either visionary or reckless.
gre.clue: either visionary or reckless

example: In an audacious move, the chess prodigy sacrificed her queen in the opening, a gamble that stunned the grandmaster across the board.

en: To criticize someone strongly and officially; such official criticism
hook: CENSURE: like a CENSOR, it officially condemns what you did.
story: Censure. To criticize someone strongly and officially; also, such official criticism. A young doctor in a northern town discovered that her hospital's director had been selling free government medicines. She reported it. After an inquiry, the health ministry formally censured the director and removed him from his post. The public censure made front-page news, and the doctor received hundreds of letters of thanks. Do not confuse censure with censor: a censor cuts words out, but censure is official blame. So, what word means to criticize someone strongly and officially? ... Censure.

gre.s: The medical board voted to ____ the surgeon for his reckless conduct, though it stopped short of revoking his license.
gre.clue: his reckless conduct

example: Parliament censured the minister after an inquiry found he had hidden the true cost of the bridge from lawmakers.

en: Polite submission and respect for another's opinion or authority
hook: DEFERENCE: you DEFER, or step aside, out of respect.
story: Deference. Polite submission and respect for another's opinion or authority. At a family meeting about a cousin's wedding, everyone had an opinion, and the voices grew loud. Then Josh's grandfather cleared his throat. The room went quiet at once, and even the eldest uncle lowered his eyes and waited. Out of deference, nobody spoke until the old man had finished. Deference comes from defer, to step aside and let someone else go first. So, what word names the respect that makes you yield to an elder's view? ... Deference.

gre.s: Out of ____ to the senior surgeon, the young resident kept her doubts to herself, a silence she later regretted.
gre.clue: kept her doubts to herself

example: In deference to her grandfather's wishes, Labiba held her wedding in the family's village home rather than a Dhaka convention hall.

en: Able to be noticed or understood, though perhaps with difficulty
bn: লক্ষণীয়; বোঝা বা দেখা যায় এমন
hook: DISCERN = to see clearly. DISCERNIBLE = can be seen.
story: Discernible. Able to be noticed or understood, though perhaps with difficulty. Far out in the Bay of Bengal, Rex's fishing boat had been at sea for six days. Through the morning haze, a thin grey line was barely discernible on the horizon. Slowly it grew into palm trees and the coast of a small island. Rex smiled and called to the crew. Home was clearly discernible at last. To discern is to see clearly, so something discernible can just be seen. So, what word describes something you can just make out, though with difficulty? ... Discernible.

gre.s: Although the forgery fooled most experts, a faint but ____ difference in the brushwork eventually gave it away.
gre.clue: eventually gave it away

example: By the third week of the new diet, there was a discernible improvement in his blood pressure, though he still felt tired.

en: Causing one to feel unsettled or uneasy
hook: DIS-CONCERT-ING: throws the CONCERT out of tune.
story: Disconcerting. Causing one to feel unsettled or uneasy. In the middle of her job interview, Nadia noticed that one interviewer had not looked up once. He kept writing and never nodded or smiled, even at her best answers. It was disconcerting, and she lost her place twice. Later she learned that he took detailed notes for everyone. To disconcert is to throw things out of concert, out of harmony, so something disconcerting knocks your calm out of tune. So, what word describes something that leaves you feeling unsettled? ... Disconcerting.

gre.s: Audiences found the film's abrupt shifts in tone ____: scenes of broad slapstick gave way, without warning, to moments of genuine brutality.
gre.clue: gave way, without warning, to moments of genuine brutality

example: It was disconcerting to hear my own voice played back on the radio, slightly higher and faster than I had imagined it.

en: Not sincere; pretending to know less than one does
hook: DIS-INGENUOUS: NOT ingenuous (innocent). Fake innocence.
story: Disingenuous. Not sincere; pretending to know less than one does. When Pam moved out of her flat, she asked the landlord for her deposit. He looked puzzled and said, "Which deposit? I never knew about any deposit." But Pam had his signed receipt in her bag. His puzzled face was completely disingenuous. She calmly took out the receipt, and [chuckle] his memory returned at once. Ingenuous means innocent and frank, and dis means not, so a disingenuous person only pretends to be innocent. So, what word describes fake innocence, pretending not to know? ... Disingenuous.

gre.s: It is ____ of the company to claim it was unaware of the defect, since internal emails show executives discussed it for months.
gre.clue: internal emails show executives discussed it for months

example: Calling the fee hike a 'small adjustment' was disingenuous, since tuition at the private university rose by nearly forty percent.

en: To tell something that was meant to stay private
hook: DIVULGE: DIVE into the secrets and BULGE them out.
story: Divulge. To tell something that was meant to stay private. For weeks, Tori's family planned a surprise party for her father's sixtieth birthday, and everyone promised to keep it secret. Then, at dinner, her little cousin [gasp] blurted out, "Is the cake chocolate or vanilla?" The secret was out. Her father [laugh] promised to act surprised anyway. The cousin had divulged everything. The root vulg comes from the Latin for common people, as in vulgar, so to divulge is to make a secret common knowledge. So, what verb means to reveal a private secret? ... Divulge.

gre.s: The journalist went to prison rather than ____ the identity of her source.
gre.clue: went to prison rather than

example: Even after ten years, my aunt refuses to divulge the secret ingredient that makes her mutton curry so famous at family weddings.

en: Refusing to give up, even when progress is slow or hard
hook: DOGGED: like a DOG holding a bone, refusing to let go.
story: Dogged. Refusing to give up, even when progress is slow or hard. Ron failed his driving test three times. The examiner frowned at his parking, his turns, his nervous hands. Each time, Ron went home, practised in an empty field at dawn, and booked the test again. On the fourth try he passed, and the examiner shook his hand. His dogged effort had paid off. Picture a dog holding a bone and refusing to let go: that is dogged determination. So, what word describes stubborn, never-give-up persistence? ... Dogged.

gre.s: Thanks to her ____ persistence, the reporter eventually uncovered the scandal that others had abandoned after a few weeks.
gre.clue: that others had abandoned after a few weeks

example: Through dogged practice every dawn on the Rajshahi riverbank, the young sprinter shaved a full second off her best time.

en: Ecstatically happy
hook: ELATED: ELEVATED with joy.
story: Elated. Ecstatically happy. When the university admission results came out, Amy's father stood in the crowd outside the gate, running his finger down the long list. Then he found her name. He [gasp] shouted, hugged a complete stranger, and [laugh] called every relative in the village, one after another. Amy had never seen him so elated, and she was elated too. Elated comes from the Latin for lifted up, and an elated person feels lifted high with joy. So, what word describes someone ecstatically happy? ... Elated.

gre.s: The team was ____ after the unexpected victory, celebrating late into the night in the streets of their small town.
gre.clue: celebrating late into the night

example: The astronomers were elated when the telescope finally captured a clear image of the comet they had tracked for six years.

en: Able to understand and share the feelings of others
hook: EMPATHETIC: feeling IN (em) someone else's pain (pathos).
story: Empathetic. Able to understand and share the feelings of others. When Zane failed his first semester exam, he sat alone in the dorm canteen, too ashamed to call home. His roommate Ivan did not lecture him. He sat down, ordered two cups of tea, and said quietly that he had failed a course in his first year too. For the first time that week, Zane felt understood. Ivan was deeply empathetic. Em means in, and path means feeling, as in sympathy, so an empathetic person feels from inside someone else's heart. So, what word describes someone who truly shares your feelings? ... Empathetic.

gre.s: The best nurses are not only technically skilled but also ____, able to sense a frightened patient's anxiety and respond to it before a word is spoken.
gre.clue: able to sense a frightened patient's anxiety

example: An empathetic coach, Sharmin noticed whenever a player was struggling at home and quietly lightened her training load.

en: Making great demands on skill, attention, or effort
bn: কঠোর পরিশ্রম দাবি করে এমন; অতি খুঁতখুঁতে
hook: EXACTING: demands everything to be EXACT.
story: Exacting. Making great demands on skill, attention, or effort. Joanna learned classical songs from an old teacher who was famously exacting. Every note had to be perfect, every word clear, every breath in the right place. One small slip, and Joanna sang the whole song again. It was exhausting, [sigh] but after five years, Joanna sang on national television. Exacting comes from exact: an exacting teacher demands that everything be exact. So, what word describes a task or a person that demands great care and effort? ... Exacting.

gre.s: The surgeon's ____ standards, which allowed no margin for error, made her residency program one of the most demanding in the country.
gre.clue: which allowed no margin for error

example: Restoring the old Armenian church in Dhaka was exacting work, as each cracked tile had to be matched by hand to the original.

en: Intensely irritated and frustrated
hook: EXASPERATED: EX-ASP, bitten by a snake of annoyance.
story: Exasperated. Intensely irritated and frustrated. Sandy had called the internet company six times in two days. Each time, a recorded voice told her to press one, then two, then wait, and then the line went dead. On the seventh call, with her online class starting in ten minutes, she [sigh] threw the phone onto the bed, completely exasperated. The root asper is Latin for rough, so exasperated means rubbed rough, like nerves scraped raw. So, what word describes someone pushed to the edge of their patience? ... Exasperated.

gre.s: After the airline cancelled his flight for the third time in a week, the ____ traveler finally gave up and rented a car.
gre.clue: for the third time in a week

example: Exasperated by the endless traffic jams on Mirpur Road, Kamal finally bought a bicycle and began riding to his office.

en: Imaginative but unrealistic
hook: FANCY-full: full of fancy imagination.
story: Fanciful. Imaginative but unrealistic. When Russell was eight, he told his friends that a giant catfish lived at the bottom of the village pond and came up only on full-moon nights to eat mangoes. His friends believed him for a whole summer. His mother [chuckle] called it one of his fanciful stories. Today Russell writes children's books, and his tales are still wonderfully fanciful. Fanciful simply means full of fancy, which is imagination. So, what word describes an idea that is imaginative but not realistic? ... Fanciful.

gre.s: The historian dismissed the legend as ____, pointing out that no record from the period mentions a sea monster at all.
gre.clue: no record from the period mentions

example: Most engineers thought his scheme of floating solar farms on every village pond was fanciful, until a pilot project actually worked.

en: Unnecessary and unjustified; given free of charge
hook: GRATUITOUS: like a GRATUITY (tip), extra and not required.
story: Gratuitous. Unnecessary and unjustified; also, given free of charge. Shelly watched a new action film with her family one Friday evening. The story was moving, but every few minutes a loud, bloody fight broke out that had nothing to do with the plot. Her father shook his head at all the gratuitous violence. Gratuitous comes from the same root as gratuity, a tip given freely without being required, so gratuitous things are extra, added for no good reason. So, what word describes something added without any good reason? ... Gratuitous.

gre.s: The reviewer's remarks about the author's appearance were entirely ____: they had no bearing on the quality of the novel and served only to humiliate her.
gre.clue: had no bearing on the quality of the novel

example: The coach's gratuitous insults after the defeat hurt the young players far more than the scoreline itself.

en: Peculiar to an individual; distinctive and unusual
hook: IDIO-SYNCRATIC: IDIO means one's own (as in idiom).
story: Idiosyncratic. Peculiar to an individual; distinctive and unusual. Toby's chemistry professor wore the same blue sweater even in the June heat, drank tea only from a steel glass, and began every lecture by quoting a line of an old folk song. His students found these habits idiosyncratic, but they loved him for them, and they still copy his quotes today. Idio means one's own, as in idiom, so an idiosyncratic habit belongs to one person alone. So, what word describes a habit that is strange and peculiar to one person? ... Idiosyncratic.

gre.s: The novelist's spelling and punctuation are so ____ that editors hesitate to correct them, fearing they would erase the very quirks that make her voice unmistakable.
gre.clue: the very quirks that make her voice unmistakable

example: The professor's idiosyncratic grading system awarded extra marks for the questions students asked rather than the answers they gave.

en: Dull and tedious because of lack of variety
hook: MONO-TONE: one tone, over and over.
story: Monotonous. Dull and tedious because of lack of variety. In a big garment factory, Rita sews the same pocket onto the same shirt, hundreds of times a day, to the same hum of machines. The work is monotonous, and the hours are long. But every evening she studies English from a small book, dreaming of a different job. Mono means one and tone means sound, so monotonous means one tone, over and over. So, what word describes work that is dull because it never changes? ... Monotonous.

gre.s: The ____ landscape, mile after mile of identical wheat fields, made the long drive feel endless.
gre.clue: mile after mile of identical wheat fields

example: The lecturer's monotonous voice, never rising or falling, sent half the back row to sleep before the tea break.

en: To force someone out of a position or place
hook: OUST: kick OUT.
story: Oust. To force someone out of a position or place. For ten years, the same man ran the market traders' association in town, collecting fees and doing very little. At last the small shopkeepers called a vote. Almost every hand went up. They ousted him and elected a young vegetable seller named Sally, and the traders [laugh] cheered as she took the chair. Oust sounds like out, and to oust someone is to push them out. So, what verb means to force someone out of power? ... Oust.

gre.s: The rebels' attempt to ____ the dictator failed when the army remained loyal to him.
gre.clue: when the army remained loyal to him

example: Shareholders voted to oust the chief executive after the company lost a third of its value in a single year.

en: To tell someone you are disappointed by what they did; such criticism
hook: REPROACH: re-APPROACH someone to tell them they disappointed you.
story: Reproach. To tell someone you are disappointed by what they did; also, such criticism. Shane came home at two in the morning, after promising to be back by ten. His mother was waiting on the sofa. She did not shout. She only said softly that she had kept his rice warm for four hours. That gentle reproach hurt more than any scolding, and he never came home late again without calling. Hear approach inside reproach: you approach someone to show how they let you down. So, what word names a quiet criticism that shows disappointment? ... Reproach.

gre.s: Rather than ____ the young employee for his mistake, the manager calmly showed him how to avoid it in the future.
gre.clue: calmly showed him how to avoid it in the future

example: My mother never shouted, but she could reproach us with a single look whenever we forgot to greet guests at the door.

en: Severely critical; harsh
hook: SCATHING: leaves you SCARRED and burned.
story: Scathing. Severely critical; harsh. Fred spent a month writing his first newspaper column about city traffic. The editor read it, picked up a red pen, and wrote a scathing note across the top: lazy, full of clichés, and boring from the very first line. Fred's ears burned. But he rewrote it five times, and the sixth version was published. To come out unscathed means to escape unharmed, so scathing words are the ones that do harm. So, what word describes criticism that is severely harsh? ... Scathing.

gre.s: The auditor's ____ report, which described the agency's management as reckless and incompetent, led to the director's immediate resignation.
gre.clue: described the agency's management as reckless and incompetent

example: The opposition leader gave a scathing speech in parliament, accusing the government of ignoring families displaced by the floods.

en: Not genuine; false or fake
hook: SPURIOUS: SPURred by lies, false.
story: Spurious. Not genuine; false or fake. A message spread through family chats, claiming that hot lemon water every hour would cure dengue. Thousands forwarded it. A young doctor named Tess went on local television to explain calmly that the claim was spurious, with no evidence at all, and that patients needed real treatment. In Latin, spurius meant false or illegitimate, so a spurious claim is a counterfeit of the truth. So, what word describes a claim that looks real but is fake? ... Spurious.

gre.s: Scholars have shown that the letter, long attributed to the queen, is ____, a forgery produced nearly a century after her death.
gre.clue: a forgery produced nearly a century after her death

example: The supplement company's spurious claim that its pills cured diabetes led the health ministry to ban the product.

en: To weaken or overturn an established system or authority, often secretly
hook: SUB-VERT: turn (vert) from below (sub), flipping the system upside down.
story: Subvert. To weaken or overturn an established system or authority, often secretly. A gang once tried to subvert the national exams by leaking question papers on social media the night before each test. Honest students who had studied for months felt cheated. Then the police traced the leaks, and the board changed how papers were printed and delivered. Sub means under and vert means turn, as in reverse, so to subvert is to turn a system over from below. So, what verb means to secretly undermine an established system? ... Subvert.

gre.s: The director's films ____ the conventions of the horror genre, revealing the monster in the first scene and making the audience sympathize with it.
gre.clue: revealing the monster in the first scene

example: Election observers accused local officials of trying to subvert the vote by moving polling stations at the last minute.

en: Accepted or suggested silently, without being put into words
hook: TACIT: TACITURN, silent agreement.
story: Tacit. Accepted or suggested silently, without being put into words. In Nadia's family, nobody ever said it aloud, but everyone knew that the best chair on the veranda belonged to Grandfather. Guests would sit there, see the family's faces, and quietly move. It was a tacit rule. Even the cat, [chuckle] it seemed, followed it. Tacit shares a root with taciturn, which describes someone who says very little, so a tacit agreement is a silent one. So, what word describes an understanding that is never spoken aloud? ... Tacit.

gre.s: Although the treaty never explicitly mentioned the disputed island, both nations had reached a ____ understanding that neither would station troops there.
gre.clue: never explicitly mentioned

example: By tacit agreement, the two brothers never mentioned their late father's debts at the dinner table.

en: To emphasize or draw attention to
hook: UNDERSCORE: draw a line UNDER a word to highlight it.
story: Underscore. To emphasize or draw attention to. Shawn's grandfather remembers the cyclones of the past, when whole villages were swept away. Today Shawn is a young engineer on the coast who helps maintain the concrete cyclone shelters. When a strong storm passed last year, his village lost no one. For Shawn, that night underscored a simple truth: preparation saves lives. To underscore is literally to draw a line under a word, and so it means to stress something. So, what verb means to emphasize a point? ... Underscore.

gre.s: Bridge collapses like last week's ____ the urgent need for the repairs that engineers have requested for years.
gre.clue: that engineers have requested for years

example: The record heat waves of recent summers underscore how urgently Dhaka needs more trees and shaded public spaces.

en: Truthfulness; accuracy
hook: VERACITY: VERy accurate. 'Vera' means true.
story: Veracity. Truthfulness; accuracy. At a village council meeting, two men told opposite stories about a land boundary. The elders turned to old Kenneth, a farmer famous for never telling a lie in seventy years. Everyone trusted his veracity completely, and when he spoke, the matter was settled. Veracity comes from the Latin verus, meaning true, as in verify. Do not confuse it with voracity, which is a huge appetite. So, what word means truthfulness? ... Veracity.

gre.s: Historians question the ____ of the memoir, noting that several events it describes could not possibly have happened.
gre.clue: could not possibly have happened

example: Before publishing the leaked photographs, the editors spent two days checking their veracity with independent forensic experts.
